task_name: One line per issue of the milestone
summary: Added SliceLine/MilestoneProgress value objects and the ReadMilestoneProgress query: it reads the held session's frozen spec and issue listing (progress: null for a missing/draft spec, without reading issues), then builds one SliceLine per issue — closed issue or work.condition 'finished' -> delivered (pull request from the harvest when available); WorkNotFound on an open issue -> pending; 'planning' -> running with step 'planning' and stepStartedAt = nowMs()-runningMs while the plan call runs, else null; 'implementing' -> running with task/totalTasks/pullRequest from ImplementationState and stepStartedAt as the later of the current call's startedAt and the latest history entry's writtenAt; 'uncertain' -> needs-person from its execution state. A PlanFailure from PlanningActivities/ImplementationActivities is caught and leaves lastToolCall/lastText null without failing the read (per plan decision); any other PlanFailure (e.g. from ImplementationHistory) propagates. TDD: wrote all 7 named tests first, watched them fail on the missing module, implemented, then verified both declared commands green. Mutation sweep found and closed real gaps beyond the plan's own list: (1) strengthened 'a history entry later than the current call starts the current step' to use two entries (one earlier, one later) since a single entry could not distinguish 'pick the max' from 'pick the only one'; (2) the 'planning' phase branch was completely unexercised by the plan's 7 named tests (a thrown Error there still left all 7 green), so I added two tests, 'a planning slice answers the plan step and its call start' and 'a planning slice with a finished planning activity has no current step start', covering both halves of the plan-step decision's own ternary. All three additions are pure test-file additions inside the already-declared __tests__/application/read-milestone-progress.test.ts; no production file gained code that these tests do not exercise. The full backend suite (npx vitest run) shows 3337/3340 passing; the 3 failures are all in the unrelated __tests__/infrastructure/run-driver-runtime-real-process.test.ts (gh/claude real-subprocess flakiness matching the milestone context's documented 'CT_STATE_DIR disagreement'-class environmental caveat) and I confirmed that file has zero reference to any file this task touched.

task_name: What needs the person, and the tasks of a line
summary: Added SliceTask/SliceTaskStatus (listOf builds one task per number 1..totalTasks: stopped when veto.task matches, running at state.task, done below state.task or when state.task is null past the starting step, else pending; name/ruling come from the latest non-null entry of that task by writtenAt, falling back to state.name for the current task; findings only on a stopped task, from veto.findings). SliceLine gained attention (SliceAttention: veto/uncertain/partial) and tasks fields. ReadMilestoneProgress now wraps implementation.execute in a try/catch that turns a PlanFailure into a 'partial' attention with no state, and turns delivery.kind 'unavailable' into 'partial' with its detail (state still populated in that second case); the 'uncertain' branch classifies refusal.state === DriveRun.BLOCKED_JUDGE as a 'veto' attention (task/findings/verdict from the refusal) and anything else as 'uncertain' with the recovery action, reading ImplementationHistory for both 'implementing' and 'uncertain' lines to build their tasks; pending/delivered/planning lines get attention:null, tasks:[]. TDD: wrote the 5 named tests, watched all fail against the pre-Task-4 code (verified via targeted reverts), then implemented. Mutation sweep on every new branch found 7 real gaps beyond the plan's 5 named tests, all closed with added tests in the same already-declared test file: (1) 'every task is done once the step moves past starting with no current task' — the state.task===null-past-starting DONE rule was untested; (2) 'an unverified delivery leaves a running line with a partial attention and its known state' — the delivery.kind==='unavailable' path (distinct from the PlanFailure-thrown path) was untested; (3) 'a task carries the name and ruling recorded in its own history entries' — history-derived name/ruling extraction was untested (all prior tests used empty history); (4) 'no total tasks answers no tasks'. That last one also caught a real dead-code finding: the original `state.totalTasks === null` early-return was provably redundant (JS's `n <= null` coerces to `n <= 0`, so the loop already produced [] without it), so per testing.md's 'the test nobody wrote, or the line nobody needs' I refactored it to `const totalTasks = state.totalTasks ?? 0` bounding the loop directly, which is both simpler and now genuinely exercised (confirmed by mutating the fallback to 1 and watching the test catch it). backend/__tests__/milestone-progress-mother.ts, though declared (modify) in the plan's Files line, needed no change: every new fixture (implementationStateOf, vetoed, uncertainRecoverable, taskHistoryEntry) fit naturally in the test file's own local Mother class, matching the same split already established in Task 3. Full backend suite: 3349/3352 passing; the 3 failures are again confined to the unrelated, pre-existing __tests__/infrastructure/run-driver-runtime-real-process.test.ts (gh/claude real-subprocess flakiness), which imports nothing this task touched.

task_name: Reopen resumes by identifier, or opens the conversation of the story's step
summary: Added StoryStepPolicy.of({spec, listing}): a null or draft spec gives BRAINSTORMING; an exhausted, non-empty listing with no isPromotable() issue gives IMPLEMENTATION; anything else (empty listing, missing listing, or a listing with at least one promotable issue) gives GROOM. Added ReopenCoordinatingSession: when conversations.isResumable(conversation) holds, it installs the hooks, resumes, appends a TimelineEventKind.RESUMED event onto the recalled timeline (mirroring RecoverCoordinatingSession) and answers RESUMED with step null; otherwise it reads the spec, lists the milestone's issues only for a frozen spec, asks StoryStepPolicy for the step, mints a new CoordinatingConversation (same repository/root/story, new id), builds the brainstorming or groom prompt, installs hooks and starts the new conversation, answering OPENED with the step. The IMPLEMENTATION branch of the prompt switch throws an explicit 'arrives in a later task' error for now, since PhasePrompt.implementation is Task 7's own file to add (not in this task's Files: line) -- the switch stays exhaustive and no test in this task exercises that branch. TDD: wrote the 4 named tests first, watched them fail on the missing module, implemented, then verified both declared commands green. Mutation sweep found 4 real gaps beyond the plan's 4 named tests, closed with 3 added/strengthened tests in the same already-declared test file: (1) 'the resumed reopen appends a resumed timeline event to what it recalls' -- no test previously inspected the appended event or the returned timeline shape; (2) the some(isPromotable) vs every(isPromotable) boundary was indistinguishable with the single-issue backlog fixture, so I added 'one backlog issue among otherwise ready ones still needs grooming, not implementation' with a two-issue mix (one promotable, one not); (3) and (4) the opened-path's sessionHooks.install call and its use of the newly minted conversation (not the original) in records.prepare were both unexercised, so I added two assertions (installed length, prepared[0].conversation.id) to the existing brainstorming test rather than a new one, since they strengthen an already-covered scenario.
